youtube_title: Crown Point's Marriage Mill: the Indiana town where Rudolph Valentino got married
body: For years, couples raced to one Indiana town to get married with no waiting. Crown Point became known as the marriage mill. Indiana had no waiting period for a marriage license, so couples from Chicago crossed the state line. On March 14, 1923, the silent film star Rudolph Valentino married Natacha Rambova in Crown Point, in a justice of the peace's office across from the courthouse. The rush faded around 1940, after Indiana tightened its marriage laws, including a required blood test. The courthouse itself went up starting in 1878. They call it the Grand Old Lady. It was once threatened with demolition for a parking lot, until residents saved it. Today it holds shops, and couples still get married there.
